title: Zendesk Basic credential strings with the email address, a template, a reference or a masked display in place of the token
summary: An email address and subdomain with no token, the documented {email_address}/token:{api_token} template, a credential string whose token is an environment reference, a masked display, and an email-address username with the separator and no token.
rationale: The email address and the subdomain identify an account and carry no token. The documented template marks where a token goes and holds none, an environment reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, a masked display has no recoverable value, and a username ending at /token with nothing after it has no secret part. Protecting any of these would redact text a reader needs, and the email address is deliberately left outside every secret span.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#246). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the texts here are identifiers, templates, references, masked text or a credential string with no token, not credential values. That a template or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Zendesk statement.

sources.supports: API tokens are auto-generated passwords in the Zendesk Admin Center. ... Basic authentication is used for API tokens. ... Use the following format for the credentials: {email_address}/token:{api_token}
Not associated with a specific Zendesk user. However, you must provide an email address for an admin, agent, or other valid user when authenticating requests.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
